Tips: thanks to Mingzhi Xiaorui for putting this together
● In a codec choice, the former is the codec format you usually see; the latter is the CodecTag used by each encoding method — think of it as a signature.
● The codec affects compression efficiency: AV1 > HEVC > AVC. Higher efficiency also demands more from the device decoder, so compatibility suffers (newer formats may not play on older devices).
★ In practice: for the best quality or compatibility with older devices pick AVC (larger files); HEVC is the balanced choice; if you want small files and your device is fast, pick AV1.
● A CodecTag labels a specific encoding method within a codec. AVC and AV1 are simple — Bilibili offers only one CodecTag each; HEVC is more complicated.
◆ In our testing, Bilibili uses three CodecTags for HEVC: hev1, hvc1 and dvh1.

• hev1 — Bilibili SDR videos, and some HDR10 videos too\n• hvc1 — Bilibili HDR10, HDR Vivid and Dolby Vision (Profile8.4) videos\n• dvh1 — Bilibili Dolby Vision (Profile5) videos; a Dolby-specific tag
❶ What is the difference between CodecTags? Does it affect the encoding?

○ Take hev1 and hvc1: the essential difference is where the file header (resolution, frame rate, etc.) is written. hev1 is more flexible — it rewrites the header before every fragment; hvc1 is fixed at the start of the video and cannot change mid-stream. That can cause tiny file-size differences, but image quality is identical at the same settings.
❷ How do HDR10, HDR Vivid and Dolby Vision (Profile5 & 8.4) differ?

○ HDR10 is the most basic HDR format: static metadata only (no dynamic colour/luminance adjustment), supporting both PQ and HLG curves — Bilibili seems to use only PQ.
○ HDR Vivid is a domestic HDR standard comparable to Dolby Vision; it supports PQ and HLG, though Bilibili seems to use only PQ, and HDR Vivid videos also output an HDR10 stream for the web and older apps.
○ Dolby Vision is the highest-standard HDR format, split into several encoding levels called Profiles; Bilibili supports the common streaming Profiles 8.4 and 5.
▷ Profile8.4 is based on the HLG curve, which lets non-Dolby-Vision devices show it as ordinary HDR10 or map it to SDR without much distortion — very compatible.
▷ Profile5 is based on the PQ curve; forced playback on unsupported devices looks washed out, and because of its special ICtCp colour space (unlike the common YCbCr) such devices show purple/green colour-mapping errors — but on supported devices Profile5 looks better than Profile8.4.

☆ So Bilibili does not deliver full Dolby Vision to every device: P8.4 is broadly supported, P5 is not. If you download a dvh1 file, check in the Bilibili app that Dolby Vision plays correctly before downloading.

We may notify you in the app to delete some or all cached videos. This can be to protect content creators and their rights or because of service adjustments, and the reason will be explained in the app.
After receiving a deletion notice, delete the specified cached video and all its copies within 24 hours (authorized reposts and compliant derivative works are excluded).
After deleting, you need to confirm in the app. You can keep using the app only after all required confirmations are done.
If you do not complete the confirmation within 15 days, your account will be frozen and you will no longer be able to use this app.

Immediately stop all BDT activity; when necessary, email all users to reclaim the video and copies within 42 hours.\nLimitation: rights holders only, with documents proving representation; BDT must be taken down from all channels (GitHub and the app site), all app versions must block further use, and an announcement must explain the issue.

This acceleration is provided by CDNs supported by Bilibili; traffic never goes through a BDT server. If downloads feel slow, tap Detect on each line and pick the fastest (or use Pick the fastest above).

Naming rules help you manage downloaded files. You can use the placeholders below to define a rule.\nFolder paths are supported: you can write a rule like “{author}/{p_title}” and the app creates the folders automatically; you do not need to handle the file type.

Naming rules are still being tested: only a few variables are available and reliability is still being checked, so problems may occur. If you find any, please report them in the community.\nExtra files (danmaku, subtitles, covers) cannot be renamed by rules yet.
